name: sar-logic-timing
description: What the synchronous SAR choice buys, measured: how much of the 62.5 ns bit cycle can be spent before the conversion breaks (0 / 40 / 50 ns of comparator-decision delay still correct, 70 ns deliberately wrong as the negative control), and that an exact-tie comparator input cannot stall the conversion -- drdy still arrives every 16 clocks.
claim: README.md#target-specification -- Latency/conversion-timing row (deterministic 16-clock conversion) and the per-cycle timing budget in spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.2 that DR-0008 rests on. Substantiates the sync-vs-async row of spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.3: 'a stalled decision corrupts one bit' (synchronous) rather than 'stalls the whole conversion' (asynchronous).
analyses: meas tran aerr_ok MAX v(ok_aerr) FROM=0.1u
meas tran aerr_lt MAX v(lt_aerr) FROM=0.1u
meas tran aerr_xl MAX v(xl_aerr) FROM=0.1u
meas tran aerr_bad MAX v(bad_aerr) FROM=0.1u
meas tran dev_tie MAX v(tie_dev) FROM=0.1u
meas tran tie_a WHEN v(tie_drdy)=1.4 RISE=2
meas tran tie_b WHEN v(tie_drdy)=1.4 RISE=7
meas tran ok_a WHEN v(ok_drdy)=1.4 RISE=2
meas tran ok_b WHEN v(ok_drdy)=1.4 RISE=7
meas tran acq_av AVG v(ok_acq) FROM=0.5u TO=8.5u
meas tran iso_av AVG v(ok_iso) FROM=0.5u TO=8.5u

abs_err_delay_0ns.description: Reference: with no added decision delay, every conversion in the run is exact. Establishes that the ramp, the expected-code closed form and the loop agree before any delay is introduced, so a nonzero result on the delayed loops is attributable to the delay.

abs_err_delay_40ns.description: THE SLACK CLAIM, spent in one place. spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.2 budgets ~22 ns of the 62.5 ns bit cycle (DAC settle + comparator decision + logic propagation) and calls the remaining ~40 ns margin. This loop hands the comparator the entire 40 ns as pure added delay and requires every conversion to still be exact -- i.e. the margin the survey computes is really available to be spent, not an artefact of the arithmetic. This is the quantitative reason DR-0008 does not need asynchronous operation: async exists to recover exactly this slack, and this measures the slack being there.

abs_err_delay_50ns.description: 80 % of the bit cycle consumed and the conversion is still exact -- the largest round delay this behavioural model measures as exact, found by bisection, not assumed. An earlier draft of this deck used 55 ns here on the (unverified) assumption that the failure edge sat at the 62.5 ns cycle boundary; running it showed a real failure (max|err| = 2 LSB). Bisecting the SAME model located the true boundary between 50 ns (exact) and 52 ns (max|err| = 1 LSB, already over the 0.5 LSB bound): the model's own RC DAC-settling network (tau = 2.56 ns, sim/sar-logic-timing/testbench/tb_sar_logic_timing.spice) consumes part of the delay budget the survey's ~40 ns slack figure treated as separate, so the measured margin is narrower than the survey's arithmetic alone suggests -- a gap attributable to this testbench's settling model, not to the synchronous architecture. See DR-0010.

abs_err_delay_70ns.description: NEGATIVE CONTROL, and the check that makes the two above falsifiable. 70 ns exceeds the 62.5 ns bit cycle, so the decision arrives after the edge meant to latch it and the conversion MUST come out wrong. A testbench in which nothing can fail proves nothing; this asserts a >= 1 LSB error rather than merely permitting one.

tie_code_deviation.description: EXACT-TIE HANDLING. Input pinned exactly on the free-MSB decision threshold (V_in = V_cm) for the whole run: the comparator is deciding a zero-amplitude input, the near-metastable case redundancy and watchdogs exist for. The code must land on one of the two adjacent codes (511 or 512) -- either is a correct answer to an exact tie -- and must not be arbitrarily wrong, which is what a tie propagating into the wrong branch of the search would produce. Gated by drdy in the underlying b-source (an earlier draft measured this unconditionally and reported a spurious 512-code deviation from the output register's power-up reset value during the ~875 ns before the first conversion's drdy, independent of whether the design was correct).

tie_conv_period_ns.description: THE CADENCE CLAIM UNDER THE TIE, which is the actual synchronous-vs-asynchronous difference (spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.3). Even with the comparator deciding a dead tie on every conversion, drdy keeps arriving exactly 16 clocks = 1000 ns apart. A self-timed loop answers this case with a timeout/watchdog because the conversion can otherwise stall; a synchronous one cannot stall by construction, and this is that property measured rather than asserted.

ok_conv_period_ns.description: same cadence on the undisturbed loop, so the tie result above is a controlled comparison rather than a single number.

acq_window_ns.description: DR-0014 ACQUISITION WINDOW, and the tight measurement of it: how long per conversion the top-plate V_cm switch is closed, i.e. how long the input actually has to settle onto the bottom plates before the sampling instant. Measured as the DUTY CYCLE of samp_tp_n averaged over eight whole conversions rather than as an edge pair, so it is an integral and is insensitive to where the timestep lands inside a 0.3 ns bridge transition; averaging a periodic waveform over whole periods is also phase-independent, so the window's start does not have to be aligned to anything. DR-0014 spends one of DR-0003's four sample clocks on isolation, so the nominal is 3 x 62.5 = 187.5 ns; the measured 187.625 ns is that plus the rise/fall delay asymmetry of the one-hot OR and its bridge. It is bounded HERE, in the 5 ns-timestep deck, because sim/adc-inl-dnl/'s one-conversion-per-point schedule rests on this window being 7.5 tau of DR-0013's 25 ns input network, and a sequencer change that quietly shortened it would move that deck's acquisition residual without moving anything that deck itself checks.

iso_gap_ns.description: DR-0014's TWO-PHASE SAMPLE: the isolation gap, and its SIGN is the ordering claim. Mean of (sel_in_n - samp_tp_n)/vdd over eight whole conversions, in ns per 1000 ns conversion. Both controls rise on the same clock edge (ph15 -> ph0), so this mean is the difference of their pulse widths, which is the lead of the top-plate switch's opening over the bottom plates leaving V_in. POSITIVE means sel_in_n falls LAST -- the input legs turn off onto an already-isolated node, which is the entire mechanism of the record. If the two were ever swapped this goes negative; if the second phase were dropped it goes to zero; neither failure can hide inside a timestep, and neither would be caught by anything else in this deck or in sim/sar-logic-functional/, whose behavioural sample-and-hold is clocked by the top-plate control by construction. The nominal is one bit cycle, 62.5 ns; the measured 62.4888 ns is that less the extra inverter the generator puts on samp_bp to keep it at the same logic depth as each cell's rel.

notes: PVT SUBSET, same justification as sim/sar-logic-functional/: this deck is rung 1 of DR-0010's fidelity ladder and contains no PDK device models, so the process and temperature axes cannot move any number in it. The supply axis is swept in full because the bridge rails, the logic thresholds and (ratiometrically) V_REF all track it. The PVT-bearing timing claim -- what the DAC settle + comparator + logic actually consume of the 62.5 ns at the slow corner -- is not this record's: DAC settling is sim/cdac-bit-settling/, comparator decision time is #9, and gf180mcu logic propagation is #12 working from a transistor-level implementation.

The delay inserted here is a lossless transmission line, not a lumped filter, so it is a pure transport delay: the measurement is 'how late may the decision be', with no shape change that would blur the failure edge.

acq_window_ns and iso_gap_ns are measured HERE rather than in sim/sar-logic-functional/, and that placement is itself a correction taken from a run. The first form of the two-phase-sample check lived in the functional deck and measured the two controls' falling edges directly (meas WHEN ... FALL=k). That deck runs 1024.5 us with a 20 ns MAXIMUM TIMESTEP, so a threshold crossing on a 0.3 ns bridge transition is interpolated from samples up to 20 ns apart: record sim/sar-logic-functional/records/20260802-094246-16ec0f1.md measured the same, unchanged, correct design as 61.28 ns at conversion 5 and 63.30 ns at conversion 500. That is the instrument's resolution, not the design's jitter. This deck runs 8.5 us at a 5 ns timestep, and the quantity is a time average over whole conversions rather than an edge pair, so the supply-axis spread of both numbers is 4e-4 % -- which is what a bound of +/- 0.3 ns needs in order to mean anything.

The delay values are a bracket, not a sweep, and were corrected by bisection during issue #11's own verification pass: an initial 0/40/55/70 ns bracket (55 ns assumed, not measured, to be 'still correct') measured a real failure at 55 ns. Bisecting between 40 and 55 ns located the true boundary between 50 ns (exact) and 52 ns (already 1 LSB over the 0.5 LSB bound); the bracket now uses 0/40/50/70 ns, with 50 ns being the largest round delay this model measures as exact rather than an assumed value.
